key_insight: Routine clinical data collected during tuberculosis treatment improves prediction of end-of-therapy status, but it is only modestly useful for predicting later relapse.
clinical_relevance: For TB trials and follow-up planning, post-baseline data can help refine risk stratification, but stronger relapse-specific biomarkers are still needed.
method: Harmonized clinical data from two Phase 3 TB trials (2,918 participants)
Monthly time-resolved models from baseline through treatment end
Compared tabular models with large language model-derived embeddings and longitudinal approaches
evidence_signal: Across the two trials, end-of-therapy prediction reached ROC-AUC up to 0.84 after month 3, while relapse prediction only improved slightly to about 0.58-0.63 by month 3 before declining.
watch_item: Performance gains for relapse were limited and some more flexible models were less interpretable, so these methods should not be treated as a substitute for relapse-specific biological markers.
paper_title: Time-resolved predictability of end-of-therapy outcome and relapse after cure in Phase 3 tuberculosis trials
